paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is really about: a proud heart stops listening. Amaziah had just beaten Edom, and Jehoash told him straight out that his heart had become "proud and boastful" (2 Chronicles 25:19). Jehoash even said to stay home, and Amaziah would not listen (2 Chronicles 25:20). I think a win can make your ears the first thing to go, and I've seen a cookie head swell bigger than the batch.

Now look at WHY he wouldn't listen. The writer says it came from God, "because they had sought the gods of Edom" (2 Chronicles 25:20). Amaziah's trouble didn't start at Beth-shemesh. It started when his heart turned away from the LORD, and the writer says it again at the end: "From the time that Amaziah turned from following the LORD…" (2 Chronicles 25:27). Pride and turning from God travel together, baker, and the fall just shows what was already going on inside.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery. When a good thing happens, stay close to the LORD and keep your ears open, even when the word comes from somebody you didn't expect. Hear the warning while it's still a warning. And this story isn't the whole Bible, friend, so keep baking, because there's more of God's Word waiting for you.
